primitive.migration_notes: C6 (2026-10-03, lancelot): two supplied-map interfaces in GTBase.edge_colourings over an eqType palette, both keeping the supplied map and its labels. SET MAPS ({set G} -> C): the public foundation source Extremal.foundations.edge_colourings.proper_ecolouring (endpoint form, eqType palette, kept public under its old name as a transparent adapter), X142 (intersection form, 'I_k) and X14 (not-disjoint form, finType) now unfold to proper_edge_colouring; the two edge-pair forms are certified by proper_edge_colouring_edgesP / proper_edge_colouring_meetP. PAIR MAPS (G -> G -> C, symmetric on ALL ordered pairs): X213 ('I_k) and D2chr.proper_ec (finType) now unfold to proper_pair_edge_colouring, by conversion. Empty-palette behaviour differs by interface and is grounded: no set map into an empty palette exists (the domain {set G} is inhabited), the empty graph admits the unique pair map into an empty palette, a nonempty edgeless graph does not (D2chr's K_1 = 1 convention). X142's numeric labels and incident sums, X213's whole-function Kempe states and used-colour count, D2chr's least star index, X229's full palette split are unchanged; M1's complete frozen X142 chain is reused (its helper certificate proof re-proved through proper_edge_colouring_edgesP) and restated by the chromatic entry point. X213's prose ('only adjacent pairs are constrained') disagrees with its body (symmetry on all pairs): recorded, not repaired. Additive B6 history composes the unchanged partial X14/X62 snapshots into complete Originals over both frozen families and raw path-edge/cover declarations; both reports verify the five new helper/statement bridges.

set-map-edge-pair-form.note: distinct edges with a nonempty intersection (X142), resp. not disjoint (X14), get different colours; both over the M1 edge-set alias of their file

pair-map-globally-symmetric.note: ordered-pair maps symmetric on every pair, adjacent or not; distinct neighbours of a vertex get different colours

distinct_variants.Chromatic.conjectures.U5.acyclic_edge_co: Embeds the pair properness clauses but adds the no-bichromatic-cycle restriction; a whole definition that is not ordinary proper edge colouring. Untouched.
distinct_variants.Chromatic.conjectures.U5.star_edge_colou: Embeds the pair properness clauses but adds the star restriction; untouched (D2chr's star_edge_colouring is a chain of this family because it calls proper_ec).
distinct_variants.Chromatic.conjectures.X43.x43_strong_edg: Distance-two edge constraint on a local line graph; untouched.
distinct_variants.Chromatic.conjectures.X219.x219_edge_cho: List assignments with membership requirements; its inlined properness belongs to a later list family. Untouched.
distinct_variants.Cycle.conjectures.X9.x9_cycle_incident_e: Constrains only the edges of a supplied sequence, not E(G). Untouched.
distinct_variants.Chromatic.conjectures.X100.x100_modular_: Permits repeated incident colours under modular degree restrictions. Untouched.

upstream_audit.note: coq-graph-theory 0.9.7 has no supplied proper-edge-colouring predicate: coloring is a partition into stable sets, mgraph.line_graph is DIRECTED (target e1 == source e2) and GTBase.base.line_graph lives on multigraph edge identities with a count-only edge_colourable, so none is a faithful canonical for the corpus' supplied maps; no line-graph bridge is claimed. The two corpus carriers are kept as two interfaces of one focused GTBase module (three areas need it): set maps {set G} -> C read on the doubletons of actual edges, and pair maps G -> G -> C symmetric on all ordered pairs, both over an eqType palette (the public foundation source already was; C5's finType vertex-colouring wrapper is not used so as not to narrow it). The set-to-pair bridge fun x y => col [set x; y] is explicit; no map on the subtype of actual edges replaces either domain, because that would admit an empty palette for every edgeless graph while the corpus domains do not.
